mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a downturn in economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which is likely to boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS shows sustained increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a weakening supply side of the economy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of the instances where INDPRO declines > 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth slows.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS declines > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where both UNRATE and PAYEMS meet the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where both HOUST and UNRATE meet the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) suggests easing inflationary pressures, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate potential monetary policy easing.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL declines > 0.2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 shows sustained increase, the hypothesis is rejected.
